external_references.url: L. Goubin. A sound method for switching between boolean and arithmetic masking. In CHES ’01: Proceedings of the Third International Workshop on Cryptographic Hardware and Embedded Systems, pages 3–15, London, UK, 2001. Springer-Verlag.

objects.name: Increase Clock Cycles/Timing
objects.description: Use more clock cycles such that branching does not affect the execution time. Also, the memory access times should be standardized to be the same over all accesses. If timing is not mission critical and time is in abundance, the access times can be reduced by adding sufficient delay to normalize the access times.  These countermeasures will result in increased power consumption which may not be conducive for low size, weight, and power missions.

objects.name: Dual Layer Protection
objects.description: Use a dual layered case with the inner layer a highly conducting surface and the outer layer made of a non-conducting material. When heat is generated from internal computing components, the inner, highly conducting surface will quickly dissipate the heat around. The outer layer prevents accesses to the temporary hot spots formed on the inner layer.

objects.name: OSAM Dual Authorization
objects.description: Before engaging in an On-orbit Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing (OSAM) mission, verification of servicer should be multi-factor authenticated/authorized by both the serviced ground station and the serviced asset.

objects.name: Communication Physical Medium
objects.description: Establish alternate physical medium for networking based on threat model/environment. For example, fiber optic cabling is commonly perceived as a better choice in lieu of copper for mitigating network security concerns (i.e., eavesdropping / traffic flow analysis) and this is because optical connections transmit data using light, they don’t radiate signals that can be intercepted.

objects.name: Protocol Update / Refactoring
objects.description: A protocol is a set of rules (i.e., formats and procedures) to implement and control some type of association (e.g., communication) between systems. Protocols can have vulnerabilities within their specification and may require updating or refactoring based on vulnerabilities or emerging threats (i.e., quantum computing).

objects.name: TRANSEC
objects.description: Utilize TRANSEC in order to prevent interception, disruption of reception, communications deception, and/or derivation of intelligence by analysis of transmission characteristics such as signal parameters or message externals. For example, jam-resistant waveforms can be utilized to improve the resistance of radio frequency signals to jamming and spoofing. Note: TRANSEC is that field of COMSEC which deals with the security of communication transmissions, rather than that of the information being communicated.

objects.name: Asset Inventory
objects.description: Asset inventorying identifies and records the organization's assets and enriches each inventory item with knowledge about their vulnerabilities.

objects.name: Configuration Inventory
objects.description: Configuration inventory identifies and records the configuration of software and hardware and their components throughout the organization.

objects.name: Data Inventory
objects.description: Data inventorying identifies and records the schemas, formats, volumes, and locations of data stored and used on the organization's architecture.

objects.name: Software Inventory
objects.description: Software inventorying identifies and records the software items in the organization's architecture.

objects.name: Asset Vulnerability Enumeration
objects.description: Asset vulnerability enumeration enriches inventory items with knowledge identifying their vulnerabilities.

objects.name: Network Node Inventory
objects.description: Network node inventorying identifies and records all the network nodes (hosts, routers, switches, firewalls, etc.) in the organization's architecture.

objects.name: Hardware Component Inventory
objects.description: Hardware component inventorying identifies and records the hardware items in the organization's architecture.

objects.name: Network Mapping
objects.description: Network mapping encompasses the techniques to identify and model the physical layer, network layer, and data exchange layers of the organization's network and their physical location, and determine allowed pathways through that network.

objects.name: Logical Link Mapping
objects.description: Logical link mapping creates a model of existing or previous node-to-node connections using network-layer data or metadata.

objects.name: Active Logical Link Mapping
objects.description: Active logical link mapping sends and receives network traffic as a means to map the whole data link layer, where the links represent logical data flows rather than physical connection

objects.name: Passive Logical Link Mapping
objects.description: Passive logical link mapping only listens to network traffic as a means to map the the whole data link layer, where the links represent logical data flows rather than physical connections.

objects.name: Network Vulnerability Assessment
objects.description: Network vulnerability assessment relates all the vulnerabilities of a network's components in the context of their configuration and interdependencies and can also include assessing risk emerging from the network's design as a whole, not just the sum of individual network node or network segment vulnerabilities.

objects.name: Physical Link Mapping
objects.description: Physical link mapping identifies and models the link connectivity of the network devices within a physical network.

objects.name: Active Physical Link Mapping
objects.description: Active physical link mapping sends and receives network traffic as a means to map the physical layer.

objects.name: Passive Physical Link Mapping
objects.description: Passive physical link mapping only listens to network traffic as a means to map the physical layer.

objects.name: Network Traffic Policy Mapping
objects.description: Network traffic policy mapping identifies and models the allowed pathways of data at the network, tranport, and/or application levels.

objects.name: Operational Activity Mapping
objects.description: Operational activity mapping identifies activities of the organization and the organization's suborganizations, groups, roles, and individuals that carry out the activities and then establishes the dependencies of the activities on the systems and people that perform those activities.,Identifying staff and organizational structure is part of operational activity mapping. One inventories assets; people are *not* assets, but are resources. Grasping operations and activities (missions) and mapping them to people is (notionally) last phase of modeling architecture.

objects.name: Access Modeling
objects.description: Access modeling identifies and records the access permissions granted to administrators, users, groups, and systems.

objects.name: Operational Dependency Mapping
objects.description: Operational dependency mapping identifies and models the dependencies of the organization's activities on each other and on the organization's performers (people, systems, and services.)  This may include modeling the higher- and lower-level activities of an organization forming a hierarchy, or layering, of the dependencies in an organization's activities.

objects.name: Operational Risk Assessment
objects.description: Operational risk assessment identifies and models the vulnerabilities of, and risks to, an organization's activities individually and as a whole.

objects.name: Organization Mapping
objects.description: Organization mapping identifies and models the people, roles, and groups with an organization and the relations between them.

objects.name: System Mapping
objects.description: System mapping encompasses the techniques to identify the organization's systems, how they are configured and decomposed into subsystems and components, how they are dependent on one another, and where they are physically located.

objects.name: Data Exchange Mapping
objects.description: Data exchange mapping identifies and models the organization's intended design for the flows of the data types, formats, and volumes between systems at the application layer.

objects.name: Service Dependency Mapping
objects.description: Service dependency mapping determines the services on which each given service relies.

objects.name: System Dependency Mapping
objects.description: System dependency mapping identifies and models the dependencies of system components on each other to carry out their function.

objects.name: System Vulnerability Assessment
objects.description: System vulnerability assessment relates all the vulnerabilities of a system's components in the context of their configuration and internal dependencies and can also include assessing risk emerging from the system's design as a whole, not just the sum of individual component vulnerabilities.

objects.name: Message Hardening
objects.description: Email or Messaging Hardening includes measures taken to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of user to user computer messages.

objects.name: Message Authentication
objects.description: Authenticating the sender of a message and ensuring message integrity.

objects.name: Message Encryption
objects.description: Encrypting a message body using a cryptographic key.

objects.name: Transfer Agent Authentication
objects.description: Validating that server components of a messaging infrastructure are authorized to send a particular message.

objects.name: Credential Hardening
objects.description: Credential Hardening techniques modify system or network properties in order to protect system or network/domain credentials.

objects.name: Biometric Authentication
objects.description: Using biological measures in order to authenticate a user.

objects.name: Certificate-based Authentication
objects.description: Requiring a digital certificate in order to authenticate a user.

objects.name: Certificate Pinning
objects.description: Persisting either a server's X509 certificate or their public key and comparing that to server's presented identity to allow for greater client confidence in the remote server's identity for SSL connections.

objects.name: Credential Transmission Scoping
objects.description: Limiting the transmission of a credential to a scoped set of relying parties.

objects.name: Domain Trust Policy
objects.description: Restricting inter-domain trust by modifying domain configuration.

objects.name: Multi-factor Authentication
objects.description: Requiring proof of two or more pieces of evidence in order to authenticate a user.

objects.name: One-time Password
objects.description: A one-time password is valid for only one user authentication.

objects.name: Strong Password Policy
objects.description: Modifying system configuration to increase password strength.

objects.name: User Account Permissions
objects.description: Restricting a user account's access to resources.

objects.name: Credential Rotation
objects.description: Expiring an existing set of credentials and reissuing a new valid set

objects.name: Platform Hardening
objects.description: Hardening components of a Platform with the intention of making them more difficult to exploit. Platforms includes components such as: * BIOS UEFI Subsystems * Hardware security devices such as Trusted Platform Modules * Boot process logic or code * Kernel software components

objects.name: Bootloader Authentication
objects.description: Cryptographically authenticating the bootloader software before system boot.

objects.name: Disk Encryption
objects.description: Encrypting a hard disk partition to prevent cleartext access to a file system.

objects.name: Driver Load Integrity Checking
objects.description: Ensuring the integrity of drivers loaded during initialization of the operating system.

objects.name: File Encryption
objects.description: Encrypting a file using a cryptographic key.

objects.name: Local File Permissions
objects.description: Restricting access to a local file by configuring operating system functionality.

objects.name: RF Shielding
objects.description: Adding physical barriers to a platform to prevent undesired radio interference.

objects.name: Software Update
objects.description: Replacing old software on a computer system component.

objects.name: System Configuration Permissions
objects.description: Restricting system configuration modifications to a specific user or group of users.

objects.name: TPM Boot Integrity
objects.description: Assuring the integrity of a platform by demonstrating that the boot process starts from a trusted combination of hardware and software and continues until the operating system has fully booted and applications are running.  Sometimes called Static Root of Trust Measurement (STRM).

objects.name: Application Hardening
objects.description: Application Hardening makes an executable application more resilient to a class of exploits which either introduce new code or execute unwanted existing code. These techniques may be applied at compile-time or on an application binary.

objects.name: Application Configuration Hardening
objects.description: Modifying an application's configuration to reduce its attack surface.

objects.name: Dead Code Elimination
objects.description: Removing unreachable or "dead code" from compiled source code.

objects.name: Exception Handler Pointer Validation
objects.description: Validates that a referenced exception handler pointer is a valid exception handler.

objects.name: Pointer Authentication
objects.description: Comparing the cryptographic hash or derivative of a pointer's value to an expected value.

objects.name: Process Segment Execution Prevention
objects.description: Preventing execution of any address in a memory region other than the code segment.

objects.name: Segment Address Offset Randomization
objects.description: Randomizing the base (start) address of one or more segments of memory during the initialization of a process.

objects.name: Stack Frame Canary Validation
objects.description: Comparing a value stored in a stack frame with a known good value in order to prevent or detect a memory segment overwrite.

objects.name: Network Traffic Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing intercepted or summarized computer network traffic to detect unauthorized activity.

objects.name: Administrative Network Activity Analysis
objects.description: Detection of unauthorized use of administrative network protocols by analyzing network activity against a baseline.

objects.name: Byte Sequence Emulation
objects.description: Analyzing sequences of bytes and determining if they likely represent malicious shellcode.

objects.name: Certificate Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing Public Key Infrastructure certificates to detect if they have been misconfigured or spoofed using both network traffic, certificate fields and third-party logs.

objects.name: Active Certificate Analysis
objects.description: Actively collecting PKI certificates by connecting to the server and downloading its server certificates for analysis.

objects.name: Passive Certificate Analysis
objects.description: ['Collecting host certificates from network traffic or other passive sources like a certificate transparency log and analyzing them for unauthorized activity.', 'Passively collecting certificates and analyzing them.']

objects.name: Client-server Payload Profiling
objects.description: Comparing client-server request and response payloads to a baseline profile to identify outliers.

objects.name: Connection Attempt Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing failed connections in a network to detect unauthorized activity.

objects.name: DNS Traffic Analysis
objects.description: Analysis of domain name metadata, including name and DNS records, to determine whether the domain is likely to resolve to an undesirable host.

objects.name: File Carving
objects.description: Identifying and extracting files from network application protocols through the use of network stream reassembly software.

objects.name: Inbound Session Volume Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing inbound network session or connection attempt volume.

objects.name: IPC Traffic Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing standard inter process communication (IPC) protocols to detect deviations from normal protocol activity.

objects.name: Network Traffic Community Deviation
objects.description: Establishing baseline communities of network hosts and identifying statistically divergent inter-community communication.

objects.name: Per Host Download-Upload Ratio Analysis
objects.description: Detecting anomalies that indicate malicious activity by comparing the amount of data downloaded versus data uploaded by a host.

objects.name: Protocol Metadata Anomaly Detection
objects.description: Collecting network communication protocol metadata and identifying statistical outliers.

objects.name: Relay Pattern Analysis
objects.description: The detection of an internal host relaying traffic between the internal network and the external network.

objects.name: Remote Terminal Session Detection
objects.description: Detection of an unauthorized remote live terminal console session by examining network traffic to a network host.

objects.name: RPC Traffic Analysis
objects.description: Monitoring the activity of remote procedure calls in communication traffic to establish standard protocol operations and potential attacker activities.

objects.name: Platform Monitoring
objects.description: Monitoring platform components such as operating systems software, hardware devices, or firmware.

objects.name: Firmware Behavior Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing the behavior of embedded code in firmware and looking for anomalous behavior and suspicious activity.

objects.name: Firmware Embedded Monitoring Code
objects.description: Monitoring code is injected into firmware for integrity monitoring of firmware and firmware data.

objects.name: Firmware Verification
objects.description: Cryptographically verifying firmware integrity.

objects.name: Peripheral Firmware Verification
objects.description: Cryptographically verifying peripheral firmware integrity.

objects.name: System Firmware Verification
objects.description: Cryptographically verifying installed system firmware integrity.

objects.name: Operating System Monitoring
objects.description: The operating system software, for D3FEND's purposes, includes the kernel and its process management functions, hardware drivers, initialization or boot logic. It also includes and other key system daemons and their configuration. The monitoring or analysis of these components for unauthorized activity constitute **Operating System Monitoring**.

objects.name: Endpoint Health Beacon
objects.description: Monitoring the security status of an endpoint by sending periodic messages with health status, where absence of a response may indicate that the endpoint has been compromised.

objects.name: Input Device Analysis
objects.description: Operating system level mechanisms to prevent abusive input device exploitation.

objects.name: Memory Boundary Tracking
objects.description: Analyzing a call stack for return addresses which point to unexpected  memory locations.

objects.name: Scheduled Job Analysis
objects.description: Analysis of source files, processes, destination files, or destination servers associated with a scheduled job to detect unauthorized use of job scheduling.

objects.name: System Daemon Monitoring
objects.description: Tracking changes to the state or configuration of critical system level processes.

objects.name: System File Analysis
objects.description: Monitoring system files such as authentication databases, configuration files, system logs, and system executables for modification or tampering.

objects.name: Service Binary Verification
objects.description: Analyzing changes in service binary files by comparing to a source of truth.

objects.name: System Init Config Analysis
objects.description: Analysis of any system process startup configuration.

objects.name: User Session Init Config Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing modifications to user session config files such as .bashrc or .bash_profile.

objects.name: Process Analysis
objects.description: Process Analysis consists of observing a running application process and analyzing it to watch for certain behaviors or conditions which may indicate adversary activity. Analysis can occur inside of the process or through a third-party monitoring application. Examples include monitoring system and privileged calls, monitoring process initiation chains, and memory boundary allocations.

objects.name: Database Query String Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing database queries to detect [SQL Injection](https://capec.mitre.org/data/definitions/66.html).

objects.name: File Access Pattern Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing the files accessed by a process to identify unauthorized activity.

objects.name: Indirect Branch Call Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing vendor specific branch call recording in order to detect ROP style attacks.

objects.name: Process Code Segment Verification
objects.description: Comparing the "text" or "code" memory segments to a source of truth.

objects.name: Process Self-Modification Detection
objects.description: Detects processes that modify, change, or replace their own code at runtime.

objects.name: Process Spawn Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing spawn arguments or attributes of a process to detect processes that are unauthorized.

objects.name: Process Lineage Analysis
objects.description: Identification of suspicious processes executing on an end-point device by examining the ancestry and siblings of a process, and the associated metadata of each node on the tree, such as process execution, duration, and order relative to siblings and ancestors.

objects.name: Script Execution Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing the execution of a script to detect unauthorized user activity.

objects.name: Shadow Stack Comparisons
objects.description: Comparing a call stack in system memory with a shadow call stack maintained by the processor to determine unauthorized shellcode activity.

objects.name: System Call Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing system calls to determine whether a process is exhibiting unauthorized behavior.

objects.name: File Creation Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing the properties of file create system call invocations.

objects.name: Message Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing email or instant message content to detect unauthorized activity.

objects.name: Sender MTA Reputation Analysis
objects.description: Characterizing the reputation of mail transfer agents (MTA) to determine the security risk in emails.

objects.name: Sender Reputation Analysis
objects.description: Ascertaining sender reputation based on information associated with a message (e.g. email/instant messaging).

objects.name: Identifier Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing identifier artifacts such as IP address, domain names, or URL(I)s.

objects.name: Homoglyph Detection
objects.description: Comparing strings using a variety of techniques to determine if a deceptive or malicious string is being presented to a user.

objects.name: URL Analysis
objects.description: Determining if a URL is benign or malicious by analyzing the URL or its components.

objects.name: Identifier Reputation Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing the reputation of an identifier.

objects.name: Domain Name Reputation Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing the reputation of a domain name.

objects.name: File Hash Reputation Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing the reputation of a file hash.

objects.name: IP Reputation Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing the reputation of an IP address.

objects.name: URL Reputation Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing the reputation of a URL.

objects.name: Identifier Activity Analysis
objects.description: Taking known malicious identifiers and determining if they are present in a system.

objects.name: User Behavior Analysis
objects.description: Analysis of user behavior and patterns for the purpose of detecting unauthorized user activity.,User behavior analytics ("UBA") as defined by Gartner, is a cybersecurity process about detection of insider threats, targeted attacks, and financial fraud. UBA solutions look at patterns of human behavior, and then apply algorithms and statistical analysis to detect meaningful anomalies from those patterns-anomalies that indicate potential threats.' Instead of tracking devices or security events, UBA tracks a system's users. Big data platforms are increasing UBA functionality by allowing them to analyze petabytes worth of data to detect insider threats and advanced persistent threats.

objects.name: Authentication Event Thresholding
objects.description: Collecting authentication events, creating a baseline user profile, and determining whether authentication events are consistent with the baseline profile.

objects.name: Authorization Event Thresholding
objects.description: Collecting authorization events, creating a baseline user profile, and determining whether authorization events are consistent with the baseline profile.

objects.name: Credential Compromise Scope Analysis
objects.description: Determining which credentials may have been compromised by analyzing the user logon history of a particular system.

objects.name: Domain Account Monitoring
objects.description: Monitoring the existence of or changes to Domain User Accounts.

objects.name: Job Function Access Pattern Analysis
objects.description: Detecting anomalies in user access patterns by comparing user access activity to behavioral profiles that categorize users by role such as job title, function, department.

objects.name: Local Account Monitoring
objects.description: Analyzing local user accounts to detect unauthorized activity.

objects.name: Resource Access Pattern Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing the resources accessed by a user to identify unauthorized activity.

objects.name: Session Duration Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing the duration of user sessions in order to detect unauthorized  activity.

objects.name: User Data Transfer Analysis
objects.description: Analyzing the amount of data transferred by a user.

objects.name: User Geolocation Logon Pattern Analysis
objects.description: Monitoring geolocation data of user logon attempts and comparing it to a baseline user behavior profile to identify anomalies in logon location.

objects.name: Web Session Activity Analysis
objects.description: Monitoring changes in user web session behavior by comparing current web session activity to a baseline behavior profile or a catalog of predetermined malicious behavior.

objects.name: File Analysis
objects.description: File Analysis is an analytic process to determine a file's status. For example: virus, trojan, benign, malicious, trusted, unauthorized, sensitive, etc.

objects.name: Dynamic Analysis
objects.description: Executing or opening a file in a synthetic "sandbox" environment to determine if the file is a malicious program or if the file exploits another program such as a document reader.

objects.name: Emulated File Analysis
objects.description: Emulating instructions in a file looking for specific patterns.

objects.name: File Content Rules
objects.description: Employing a pattern matching rule language to analyze files.

objects.name: File Hashing
objects.description: Employing file hash comparisons to detect known malware.

objects.name: Network Isolation
objects.description: Network Isolation techniques prevent network hosts from accessing non-essential system network resources.

objects.name: Broadcast Domain Isolation
objects.description: Broadcast isolation restricts the number of computers a host can contact on their LAN.

objects.name: DNS Allowlisting
objects.description: Permitting only approved domains and their subdomains to be resolved.

objects.name: DNS Denylisting
objects.description: Blocking DNS Network Traffic based on criteria such as IP address, domain name, or DNS query type.

objects.name: Forward Resolution Domain Denylisting
objects.description: Blocking a lookup based on the query's domain name value.

objects.name: Hierarchical Domain Denylisting
objects.description: Blocking the resolution of any subdomain of a specified domain name.

objects.name: Homoglyph Denylisting
objects.description: Blocking DNS queries that are deceptively similar to legitimate domain names.

objects.name: Forward Resolution IP Denylisting
objects.description: Blocking a DNS lookup's answer's IP address value.

objects.name: Reverse Resolution Domain Denylisting
objects.description: Blocking a reverse DNS lookup's answer's domain name value.

objects.name: Reverse Resolution IP Denylisting
objects.description: Blocking a reverse lookup based on the query's IP address value.

objects.name: Encrypted Tunnels
objects.description: Encrypted encapsulation of routable network traffic.

objects.name: Network Traffic Filtering
objects.description: Restricting network traffic originating from any location.

objects.name: Inbound Traffic Filtering
objects.description: Restricting network traffic originating from untrusted networks destined towards a private host or enclave.

objects.name: Outbound Traffic Filtering
objects.description: Restricting network traffic originating from a private host or enclave destined towards untrusted networks.

objects.name: Execution Isolation
objects.description: Execution Isolation techniques prevent application processes from accessing non-essential system resources, such as memory, devices, or files.

objects.name: Executable Allowlisting
objects.description: Using a digital signature to authenticate a file before opening.

objects.name: Executable Denylisting
objects.description: Blocking the execution of files on a host in accordance with defined application policy rules.

objects.name: Hardware-based Process Isolation
objects.description: Preventing one process from writing to the memory space of another process through hardware based address manager implementations.

objects.name: IO Port Restriction
objects.description: Limiting access to computer input/output (IO) ports to restrict unauthorized devices.

objects.name: Kernel-based Process Isolation
objects.description: Using kernel-level capabilities to isolate processes.

objects.name: Mandatory Access Control
objects.description: Controlling access to local computer system resources with kernel-level capabilities.

objects.name: System Call Filtering
objects.description: Configuring a kernel to use an allow or deny list to filter kernel api calls.

objects.name: Decoy Environment
objects.description: A Decoy Environment comprises hosts and networks for the purposes of deceiving an attacker.

objects.name: Connected Honeynet
objects.description: A decoy service, system, or environment, that is connected to the enterprise network, and simulates or emulates certain functionality to the network, without exposing full access to a production system.

objects.name: Integrated Honeynet
objects.description: The practice of setting decoys in a production environment to entice interaction from attackers.

objects.name: Standalone Honeynet
objects.description: An environment created for the purpose of attracting attackers and eliciting their behaviors that is not connected to any production enterprise systems.

objects.name: Decoy Object
objects.description: A Decoy Object is created and deployed for the purposes of deceiving attackers.

objects.name: Decoy File
objects.description: A file created for the purposes of deceiving an adversary.

objects.name: Decoy Network Resource
objects.description: Deploying a network resource for the purposes of deceiving an adversary.

objects.name: Decoy Persona
objects.description: Establishing a fake online identity to misdirect, deceive, and or interact with adversaries.

objects.name: Decoy Public Release
objects.description: Issuing publicly released media to deceive adversaries.

objects.name: Decoy Session Token
objects.description: An authentication token created for the purposes of deceiving an adversary.

objects.name: Decoy User Credential
objects.description: A Credential created for the purpose of deceiving an adversary.

objects.name: File Eviction
objects.description: File eviction techniques evict files from system storage.

objects.name: File Removal
objects.description: The file removal technique deletes malicious artifacts or programs from a computer system.

objects.name: Email Removal
objects.description: The email removal technique deletes email files from system storage.

objects.name: Credential Eviction
objects.description: Credential Eviction techniques disable or remove compromised credentials from a computer network.

objects.name: Account Locking
objects.description: The process of temporarily disabling user accounts on a system or domain.

objects.name: Authentication Cache Invalidation
objects.description: Removing tokens or credentials from an authentication cache to prevent further user associated account accesses.

objects.name: Credential Revoking
objects.description: Deleting a set of credentials permanently to prevent them from being used to authenticate.

objects.name: Process Eviction
objects.description: Process eviction techniques terminate or remove running process.

objects.name: Process Termination
objects.description: Terminating a running application process on a computer system.

objects.name: Process Suspension
objects.description: Suspending a running process on a computer system.

objects.description: ['Attacks on critical software subsystems', 'Attitude Determination and Control (AD&C) subsystem determines and controls the orientation of the satellite. Any cyberattack that could disrupt some portion of the control loop - sensor data, computation of control commands, and receipt of the commands would impact operations', 'Telemetry, Tracking and Commanding (TT&C) subsystem provides interface between satellite and ground system. Computations occur within the RF portion of the TT&C subsystem, presenting cyberattack vector', 'Command and Data Handling (C&DH) subsystem is the brains of the satellite. It interfaces with other subsystems, the payload, and the ground. It receives, validate, decodes, and sends commands to other subsystems, and it receives, processes, formats, and routes data for both the ground and onboard computer. C&DH has the most cyber content and is likely the biggest target for cyberattack.', 'Electrical Power Subsystem (EPS) provides, stores, distributes, and controls power on the satellite. objects.description: ['Masquerading as an authorized entity in order to gain access/Insider Threat']
objects.x_aerospace_high_level_requirement: The Program shall establish policy and procedures to prevent individuals (i.e., insiders) from masquerading as individuals with valid access to areas where commanding of the spacecraft is possible.

objects.name: SV-AV-7
objects.description: ['The TT&C is the lead contributor to satellite failure over the first 10 years on-orbit, around 20% of the time. The failures due to gyro are around 12% between year one and 6 on-orbit and then ramp up starting around year six and overtake the contributions of the TT&C subsystem to satellite failure. Need to ensure equipment is not counterfeit and the supply chain is sound.']

objects.x_aerospace_high_level_requirement: The Program shall ensure security requirements/configurations are placed on the development environments to prevent the compromise of source code from supply chain or information leakage perspective.

objects.name: SV-SP-2
objects.description: ['Testing only focuses on functional requirements and rarely considers end to end or abuse cases']
objects.x_aerospace_high_level_requirement: The Program shall establish robust procedures and technical methods to perform testing to include negative testing (i.e., abuse cases) of the spacecraft hardware and software.

objects.name: SV-SP-4
objects.description: ['General supply chain interruption or manipulation']
objects.x_aerospace_high_level_requirement: The Program shall protect against supply chain threats to the spacecraft by employing security safeguards.

objects.description: ['Hardware failure (i.e., tainted hardware) {ASIC and FPGA focused}']
objects.x_aerospace_high_level_requirement: The Program shall establish robust procedures and technical methods to prevent the introduction of tainted ASIC and FPGAs into the spacecraft supply chain.
